summary: Desktop app that uses AI source separation models to remove or isolate vocals and instruments from songs, with installers for Windows and macOS.

heroCommands.command: Download UVR_v5.6.0_setup.exe from the v5.6 release
Download the arm64 or x86_64 DMG from the v5.6 release

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Ultimate Vocal Remover (UVR) is a graphical app that separates audio into parts, such as vocals and instrumentals, using state-of-the-art source separation models. The core developers trained most of the bundled models, and Demucs v3 and v4 4-stem models are included too.
sixtySeconds.problem: Isolating a vocal or making an instrumental from a finished song normally needs the original recording stems. UVR does it with AI models in a simple interface.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an all-in-one installer with Python, PyTorch and models bundled, so no setup is needed on Windows or macOS.
requirements: Windows 10+ (install to the C: drive), macOS Big Sur+, or Debian/Arch Linux for a manual install

overview: The Windows and macOS bundles include the interface, Python, PyTorch and other dependencies, so there are no prerequisites. On Windows, install UVR to the main C: drive. AMD Radeon and Intel Arc users can try the DirectML build.
On macOS, pick the arm64 DMG for Apple Silicon or the x86_64 DMG for Intel. Linux users follow a manual install using ffmpeg, Python and Tk on Debian or Arch-based systems.
Without FFmpeg, non-WAV files can't be converted. The code is MIT licensed; credit UVR if you use its models in your own app.
